title: A Can of Worms
gist_ar: نص عن استخدام التعبيرات المجازية: المجاز بيوقف التفكير بدل ما يشرحه.
text:
The minutes record that the committee agreed the matter was "a grey area" and
resolved not to "open a can of worms". Both phrases are doing something more
specific than they appear to, and it is worth getting to the bottom of what.

A grey area, taken literally, is a region where a rule does not determine an
outcome. Used figuratively, and it is nearly always used figuratively, it more
often describes a region where the rule is perfectly clear and applying it would
be costly. The connotation is of intellectual difficulty. The function is
permission to stop. That is a double-edged sword: the phrase is genuinely useful
where ambiguity is real, and it is precisely because it is useful that it works
so well when it is not.

"A can of worms" is more candid, in a way. It concedes that further enquiry would
find something. The undertone is not that the question is hard but that the
answer would be inconvenient, and the metaphor is chosen — one may infer — by
people who would rather not be quoted saying so.

By and large this is how such expressions earn their place. They evoke a shared
attitude while committing nobody to a proposition. In the long run they also
shape what a committee is able to notice, since a matter filed as grey is not
filed as unresolved, and only one of those two categories generates a review
date.

None of which is an argument for banning idiom, an allusion-free prose being both
unreadable and no more honest. It is an argument for reading the minutes
figuratively. What was actually decided here was not to look, and the phrase that
shed light on it is the one nobody drafted carefully.

questions.q: What does the writer say 'a grey area' usually does in practice?
questions.q_ar: إيه وظيفة 'منطقة رمادية' عمليًا حسب الكاتب؟
options: Describes genuine ambiguity in a rule
Gives permission to stop, where the rule is clear but costly to apply
Signals that a review date is needed

questions.q: Why does the writer call 'a can of worms' more candid?
questions.q_ar: ليه الكاتب قال إن 'فتح باب لا يُغلق' أكثر صراحة؟
options: It is a far more common expression in committee minutes than 'a grey area' is
It appears in the formal minutes
It concedes that further enquiry would find something

questions.q: What is the long-term effect the writer identifies?
questions.q_ar: إيه الأثر طويل المدى اللي حدّده الكاتب؟
options: A matter filed as 'grey' generates no review date, so it is not noticed again

questions.q: What is the writer's position on idiom generally?
questions.q_ar: إيه موقف الكاتب من التعبيرات المجازية عمومًا؟
options: It should be banned from official documents
It is only acceptable in speech and should be edited out of every written record
Prose without it would be unreadable and no more honest
